div.p: It is a thankless job—living day to day by your chainsword and the skill of your arm, by your faith in the Emperor and your refusal to surrender to the darkness. To dive heedlessly into danger, to charge into the maw of death itself, to stand between your squad and the horrors that hunger for their souls. They won't be playing golden horns for the time you took that Catachan Devil's claw to the ribs for them. No flock of angels to sing of the time you dragged them, still screaming, from the jaws of a death-spider, no hymns of praise for your sacrifice.
Forget them. Their gratitude means nothing. Their praise is empty. You don't fight for recognition. You fight for the Emperor.

You do this for the guts and the glory, for the scream of battle and the hot, hot blood of it, for the moment when your chainsword bites into xenos flesh and the Emperor's will is made manifest. You are a beast of iron, forged in the crucible of endless horror, your soul hardened by the constant struggle against the darkness. Your squad may carry lasguns and heavy weapons but, close combat specialist, you are the chainsword, the instrument of the Emperor's wrath made flesh. While your squadmates might moan about their wounds over a bivouac in the jungle, you bear your scars with pride, each one a testament to a death you cheated, a horror you survived.

You are the wall—let every danger smash itself to nothing on you. In the end, you will be the last one standing, your chainsword still roaring, your faith still burning, your soul still serving the Emperor's will even as the darkness closes in.
Catachan: Blade, Butcher, Gore, Kane, Quinn, Rix, Shredder, Slash, Tex, Zane

Hard Eyes, Dead Eyes, or Eager Eyes
Wild Hair, Shorn Hair, or Battered Helm

Body.p: When you attack with a melee weapon, add +1d6 damage.

div.p: Choose your fighting style and gain the corresponding move:
When you charge into melee combat, you may roll+Strength instead of Weapon Skill for your first attack.
Choose one weapon—you can always treat weapons of that type as if they had the precise tag.
When you press on and get in close to an enemy, take +1.
Once per battle you may reroll a single damage roll (yours or someone else's).
You start with these moves:
When you use pure strength to destroy an inanimate obstacle, roll+Strength. ✴On a 10+, choose 3. ✴On a 7-9 choose 2.

ul.li: It doesn't take a very long time
It doesn't make an inordinate amount of noise
You can fix the thing again without a lot of effort

div.p: You ignore the clumsy tag on armor you wear.

This is your chainsword. There are many like it, but this one is yours. Your chainsword is your best friend. It is your life. You master it as you master your life. Your chainsword, without you, is useless. Without your chainsword, you are useless. You must wield your chainsword true.

Choose the range that best fits your weapon:
Choose two enhancements:
Choose a look:
Defend those weaker than you.
Defeat a worthy opponent.
Complete a mission objective.
Your load is 12+Strength. You carry your chainsword and rations (5 uses, 1 weight). Choose your defenses:

ul.li: Flak armor (1 armor, 1 weight) and field gear (1 weight)

ul.li: Antitoxin (0 weight), rations (1 weight), and field dressings (1 weight)

div.p: When you gain a level from 2-5, choose from these moves.
When you deal damage, deal +1d4 damage.

When you consult the spirits that reside within your signature weapon, they will give you an insight relating to the current situation, and might ask you some questions in return, roll+Leadership. ✴On a 10+, the GM will give you good detail. ✴On a 7-9, the GM will give you an impression.

When you make your armor take the brunt of damage dealt to you, the damage is negated but you must reduce the armor value of your armor or shield (your choice) by 1. The value is reduced each time you make this choice. If the reduction leaves the item with 0 armor it is destroyed.
Choose one extra enhancement for your signature weapon.
When you discern realities during combat, you take +1.
When you parley using threats of impending violence as leverage, you may use Strength instead of Leadership.
When you engage in melee combat with an enemy, your next attack against that same foe deals +1d4 damage.
Get one move from another class. Treat your level as one lower for choosing the move.
You gain +1 armor.

When you have access to a forge you can graft the magical powers of a weapon onto your signature weapon. This process destroys the magical weapon. Your signature weapon gains the magical powers of the destroyed weapon.
When you gain a level from 6-10, choose from these moves or the level 2-5 moves.
Replaces: Merciless
When you deal damage, deal +1d8 damage.
Replaces: Armor Mastery

When you choose to let your armor take the brunt of damage dealt to you, the damage is negated and you take Advantage against the attacker, but you must reduce the armor value of your armor or shield (your choice) by 1. The value is reduced each time you make this choice. If the reduction leaves the item with 0 armor it is destroyed.
Requires: Seeing Red

When you enter combat, roll+Leadership. ✴On a 10+, hold 2. ✴On a 7-9, hold 1. Spend your hold to make eye contact with an NPC present, who freezes or flinches and can’t act until you break it off. ✴On a 6-, your enemies immediately identify you as their biggest threat.
Replaces: Scent of Blood
When you engage in melee combat with an enemy, your next attack against that same foe deals +1d8 damage.
Requires: Multiclass Dabbler
Get one move from another class. Treat your level as one lower for choosing the move.
Replaces: Iron Hide
You gain +2 armor.

When you go into battle, roll+Willpower. ✴On a 10+, name someone who will live and someone who will die. ✴On a 7-9, name someone who will live or someone who will die. Name NPCs, not player characters. The GM will make your vision come true, if it’s even remotely possible. ✴On a 6- you see your own death and consequently take Disadvantage throughout the battle.
When you look over an enemy’s weaponry, ask the GM how much damage they do.
When you engage in melee combat on a 12+ you deal your damage, avoid their attack, and impress, dismay, or frighten your enemy.

When you choose to go out in a blaze of glory at death's door, your chainsword becomes an extension of your final will. You may make one last attack against any enemy you can see, or charge through multiple enemies in a final rampage. Roll+Weapon Skill. ✴On a 10+, you deal your damage+3d12 to your primary target, ignoring all armor. The enemy is utterly destroyed. You may also deal your damage+2d10 to up to three additional enemies in your path, ignoring armor. All allies take Advantage and +1 armor for the rest of the battle. Your chainsword's final roar becomes a legend—enemies within earshot must press on or flee. ✴On a 7-9, you deal your damage+2d10 to your target, ignoring armor, and your damage+1d10 to one additional enemy. All allies take Advantage for the rest of the battle. ✴On a miss, you still deal your damage+1d10 to your target, ignoring armor. Your final strike becomes a legend that inspires your allies—they all take Advantage and +1 armor for the rest of the battle. Your death is remembered, and your chainsword's final roar echoes across Catachan, granting all future Close Combat Specialists +1 forward when they enter combat.
